subject: SLA exception request: preview model launches and beta features

Cc: procurement@acme.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA coverage for preview models in upcoming pilot

Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency on the embedding flow looked promising. We're preparing a short pilot for our internal search product next month and procurement has asked whether Redwood can provide an SLA that specifically covers new model rollouts and any features labeled as "preview" or "beta." Our legal team wants to avoid an open window where we can't rely on uptime/latency SLOs during model launches.

Specifically, they're asking for:
- Confirmation whether preview/beta features are covered under Redwood's standard 99.9% uptime and 95th/99th percentile latency SLOs.
- If not, what exception language would look like and whether we can negotiate a time-limited commitment for our pilot (6 weeks).
- A point of contact for escalation if a new model launch causes production regressions.

I've attached our internal exception request form. Can we get a draft response this week? We're on a tight procurement schedule.

Best,
Jordan Park
Senior Procurement Manager
Acme AI

Jordan — thanks for the clear note and the timeline. Looping in Vivek (engineering) and Laura (legal) so we can give a concise, negotiated position. Quick answers up front:

- By default, features explicitly labeled "preview" or "beta" and new unvetted model variants are excluded from our standard production SLA. We do this to protect customers from untested regressions and to preserve safety controls in the early rollout window.
- That said, we do offer time-limited exception language for named pilots where we can commit to scoped SLOs with technical guardrails and rollback policies.

Next steps we propose:
1) Vivek to outline the technical caveats and the minimum monitoring/rollback commitments we need.
2) Laura to propose contract language for a 6-week pilot exception (limited to specified model ids/endpoint routes).
3) Rishi to propose the operational runbook and escalation contact.

If Acme can provide the exact model ids (or confirm "any preview model") and the expected QPS, we can put together a draft this afternoon.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: SLA coverage for preview models in upcoming pilot

Jordan, Marissa — providing technical context below. TL;DR: we can provide a scoped uptime and latency commitment for a 6-week pilot, but it will require explicit constraints and automated rollback triggers.

Key constraints for any SLA exception on preview models:
- Scope by model id and route: we will only guarantee SLOs for the exact model version(s) you enumerate. Any subsequent model swap or auto-upgrade will void the exception unless pre-approved.
- Traffic caps: to avoid noisy neighbor effects we will cap the QPS for the exception (we can raise caps with dedicated capacity). Please share expected peak and average QPS.
- Monitoring requirements: Acme must ingest and retain our telemetry links for the duration of the pilot (we provide a read-only dashboard). We require 48h notice window for rollback on a model variant showing regression on quality or latency.
- Fallback policy: if a preview launch causes a latency spike or error rate above thresholds (we can propose p95>350ms or error_rate>1%), Redwood will automatically route traffic to the prior stable model variant for the affected route. That fallback action will be considered adherence to the exception SLA.

Operational items we need from Acme to finalize:
1) List of model ids/endpoints to include.
2) Pilot time window and expected QPS pattern.
3) A named on-call/contact for post-deploy escalations (email + phone).

I attached a short CSV with the preview feature compatibility checklist we use internally — helps speed negotiation.

— Vivek Kulkarni
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime
vivek.k@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood-preview-features-list.csv (text/csv, 6KB)

Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.k@redwood.ai>, rishi_mmalhotra <rishi.m@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SLA coverage for preview models in upcoming pilot

Jordan — putting a short contractual framing here so procurement has language to review. We can offer: 

- A 6-week "Pilot Exception Addendum" appended to the master services agreement. The addendum will: 
  * Enumerate covered model ids/endpoints.
  * Specify the scoped SLOs (example: 99.5% uptime for the listed endpoints; p95 latency target of <=350ms; p99 as advisory).
  * Include explicit exclusion clauses: any third-party model provided by Acme or any auto-upgrade mechanism not pre-approved will be excluded.
  * Define rollback/fallback behavior as a compliance action (i.e., an automated fallback will not be treated as an SLA breach if executed per runbook).
  * Require a short pilot-specific indemnity carve-out and an agreed-to liability cap tied to the pilot's spend.

- We will mark the addendum as time-limited: it will expire automatically at the end of the pilot window unless both parties agree in writing to extend.

If Acme prefers different SLO numbers (e.g., 99.9%) we can explore that but it will likely require Dedicated capacity or a higher spend commitment.

I'll draft the addendum and circulate an initial redline by EOD for Acme procurement to review.

— Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.b@redwood.ai

Jordan — operational notes from CS to make this practical during the pilot: 

- We'll assign a named Technical Account Lead (TAL) for the pilot window and include a 24x7 escalation contact for the first 72 business hours after any model swap.
- We'll maintain a short runbook (shared Google doc) with the rollback criteria Vivek outlined. The runbook will include automated alerts to both teams and a one-click rollback action that we can exercise if thresholds are exceeded.
- For observability, Acme will get a dashboard with token-level cost/latency breakdown and per-route traces for the covered endpoints. We recommend keeping synthetic traffic running during launch windows to detect regressions early.

If you can confirm the pilot start date (proposed March 2) and the model ids, I’ll lock in TAL assignment.
